result.title: MORSE: Optimizing Streaming Memory Design via Open-World Auto-Research
result.summary: A streaming video system must decide in a single pass what evidence to retain under bounded frame storage, before it knows which details a future question will require. Recent recursive self-improvement methods automate the design of the harness that stores and retrieves this evidence. They revise the harness in response to failures, but the editor must still devise each repair from its prior knowledge and a predefined set of tools. A failure that recurs across videos, however, may point to a problem that prior work has already addressed. We introduce MORSE (Memory Optimization with Recursive Self-Evolvement), an open-world auto-research framework that uses recurring failures to guide an online search for solutions. Its editor groups failures in training traces by cause, then searches papers, model cards, and code for methods it can adapt or pretrained perception models it can use. When the editor introduces a new perceptual capability, it can also revise how the harness stores and retrieves the resulting evidence for a frozen video-language model. On held-out validation streams, MORSE first selects revisions that improve answer quality, then seeks faster revisions that preserve those gains within a specified tolerance. Across three streaming video benchmarks, MORSE consistently achieves the highest answer accuracy within each frozen-backbone comparison. On OVO-Bench, our Qwen3-VL-8B harness answers queries in 0.30 seconds on average while achieving 75.1% accuracy, 3.1 percentage points ahead of the next-best evaluated harness using the same frozen backbone.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MORSE：以训练轨迹中反复出现的失败为线索，在线检索论文、模型卡和代码，自动修订流式视频系统的记忆 harness（证据保留与检索方式，并可引入预训练感知模型），再在冻结 VLM 上按答案质量与延迟逐级筛选修订。
AI.relevance_reason: 「有限帧存储下单遍决定保留何种证据」及按失败原因筛选、检索证据的循环，与 LVR 关注的视觉证据筛选和获取证据决策有直接交集，可供核查；但其优化对象是外部 streaming memory harness 而非模型内部 latent 状态，机制迁移性需读原文确认。
